title: The BBC Once Said Spaghetti Grows on Trees
hook: On April Fools' Day 1957, hundreds of Britons called to ask how to grow a spaghetti tree
summary: On April Fools' Day 1957 the BBC aired a report of a Swiss family harvesting spaghetti from trees, and hundreds of viewers asked how to grow their own.

text: In 1957 Britain, plenty of people had no idea.
Back then spaghetti was an exotic food in Britain.
it's made from flour and water.
On April 1 that year, the BBC current-affairs show Panorama
It showed a family in southern Switzerland harvesting spaghetti from trees.
The film showed a harvest festival in Ticino, in southern Switzerland.
The picturesque scenery made it more believable.
The voice-over was by respected broadcaster Richard Dimbleby.
He is said to have gladly lent his authority

panels.text: If a trustworthy guy says it, you just believe it

text: An estimated eight million people watched.
The next day hundreds phoned in
to question it or ask how to grow their own.

panels.text: Stick a sprig of spaghetti in the tin and hope for the best
